name: BCD to 7-Segment Display Driver
title: BCD to 7-Segment Display Driver
summary: A BCD to 7-Segment Decoder translates 4-bit Binary Coded Decimal inputs (0000 to 1001) into signals that drive 7 LED segments (a, b, c, d, e, f, g) to display numbers 0-9.

images.title: 7-Segment Layout
images.caption: Segment labelling (a, b, c, d, e, f, g) on a 7-segment display.

working_principle: Each segment is driven by a Boolean function derived using Karnaugh Maps for BCD values 0 to 9. Inputs above 9 (1010 to 1111) are 'Don't Care' conditions.
boolean_equation: Segment a = A + C + BD + B'D'
advantages: Direct decimal visual readout from binary/BCD counters
disadvantages: Requires 7 separate output driver lines per digit
common_mistakes: Confusing Common-Anode (+5V common) with Common-Cathode (GND common) displays.
quick_notes: Common Anode requires active-LOW segment outputs (0 turns LED ON).
Common Cathode requires active-HIGH segment outputs (1 turns LED ON).

viva_questions.q: What is the difference between Common Anode and Common Cathode 7-segment displays?
viva_questions.a: Common Anode connects all LED anodes to +5V (active-low drive). Common Cathode connects all LED cathodes to GND (active-high drive).

interview_questions.q: What segments are lit to display the decimal digit '7'?
